newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU transport ministers reach aircraft checks deal.
newsitem.headline: EU transport ministers reach aircraft checks deal.

text.p: European Union transport ministers struck a deal on Tuesday allowing national civil aviation authorities to inspect non-EU aircraft using their airports and ground dangerous ones.
"We have political agreement," one EU diplomat told reporters, adding that formal agreement would come only after European parliamentary approval.

Britain, Germany and Sweden had wanted the same rules to apply to EU aircraft but dropped their request in return for a reference to separate rules, at least as strict, which are already in place for EU carriers.

Tougher ramp checks form part of ministers' increased efforts to improve air safety since February 1996, when a Birgen Air crash off the Dominican Republic killed 189 people, most of them German tourists.
United States and Dominican investigators blamed the crash on human error.

According to a draft text of the rules, aircraft, their operation and crew will be subject to checks "whenever there is reasonable suspicion that international safety standards are not met" with the possibility that aircraft be grounded "if this is necessary to ensure immediate safety".

The rules, once formalised, will mean authorities must collect and share the data necessary to ensure safety norms are met. They will also require that suitable measures are found to rectify any defect.

Ministers also talked on Tuesday about the possibility of creating a European organisation for civil aviation safety and of improving the existing system of air traffic management and control in west European skies.
